page_text: Commercial summary: annual value 7.85M USD, committed annual base 7.62M USD, signed 15 Jul 2024, term 1 Aug 2024 to 31 Jul 2027, renewal notice due 30 Apr 2027.

Rights and protections: buyer may audit invoice, resource, ticket, SLA, change order, runbook, and knowledge-transfer evidence. Benchmarking may compare rate card, offshore mix, automation coverage, SLA credits, and tower scope.

Statement of work purpose: run, support, release, quality, and minor-enhancement services for the legacy analytics estate supporting clinical reporting, claims operations, finance close, member-service analytics, and executive reporting.

In-scope systems: SQL reporting marts, Tableau, Power BI semantic models, SAS analytics estate, Epic Clarity extracts, claims administration extracts, finance close marts, and ServiceNow ITSM integration.

Delivery towers: production support, data engineering run, BI sustainment, and governance evidence. Recurring fixes to named production systems remain base run work unless a written exception is approved.

Resource model: 51.8 total FTE across 15 role categories, split 9.8 onshore and 42.0 offshore, with named accountability for service delivery, platform architecture, clinical data, claims data, BI, release, security, QA, triage, and automation.
Pricing schedule: monthly base, monitoring/tooling allowance, transition and knowledge reserve, service-management overhead, and approved minor-enhancement capacity reconcile to annual value.

Role rate card: resource model billed labor is 7.1795M USD; vendor labor cost basis is 4.392M USD; labor margin and overhead bridge is 2.7875M USD before tooling, transition, and service-management overhead.

AP invoice extract: 56 invoice lines across 12 months separate base run support, governance, operations tooling, variable run support, and change-order lines. Monthly invoice line totals tie to monthly spend rows.
Change-order billing evidence: invoice lines include approved change-order charges in 2025-08, 2025-09, 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-05, and 2026-06 for scope-posture review.
SLA history: analytics service requests resolved within SLA had a 95 percent committed threshold. Breach months are 2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-04, and 2026-07.
Service-credit math: breached months carry 63,500 USD of total credit owed, credit_claimed is false on each breached row, and credit_recovered_usd remains zero.
Ticket and batch operations: monthly ServiceNow ticket volumes and batch job volumes are tied to the same periods so Source can distinguish performance leakage from generic cost cutting.

Change-order register: eight change orders separate run, transform, and reporting work. Five rows are marked in_scope_disputed because they look like recurring run work sold back as one-off project activity.
Scope posture rule: Source may prepare a challenge packet for recurring run-support change orders, but it may not label the amount as realized savings before buyer approval and finance confirmation.

QBR scorecard: run share rises from 81 percent to 88 percent, transform share falls from 19 percent to 12 percent, automation backlog grows from 31 to 48 items, and report-retirement candidates grow from 18 to 34.
Executive interpretation: the pattern supports a negotiation candidate around automation, report rationalization, and service credits, not a finance-confirmed savings claim.

Operational evidence pack: Procurement provides contract register and SOW; IT Finance provides AP invoice extracts; Service Management provides ServiceNow ticket exports; Technology Platform provides CMDB; Vendor Management provides change orders; Analytics Operations provides QBR scorecards.
Load rule: Layer 1 files must be loaded through adapters. Product surfaces cannot read this package directly, and missing source rows block related executive claims rather than being estimated.
